title: Service-sidecar buffered span aggregator with per-route adaptive sampling
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Our tracer SDKs still cause significant allocations and syscall overhead on hot request paths despite previous tail-sampling improvements. Observed symptoms: p50 token latency spikes on high-QPS endpoints when tracing is enabled, CPU pressure from frequent JSON serialization, and occasional exporter backpressure that increases application tail latency.

Goal: Implement a service-sidecar buffered span aggregator that shifts batching, sampling-decisions, and final serialization off the hot path in the application SDK. Support per-route adaptive sampling rules so we can apply aggressive sampling for noisy internal routes while preserving full fidelity for customer-facing flows. The change should reduce allocations and syscall frequency in the SDK path, keep end-to-end trace fidelity for high-impact requests, and provide a safe rollout path with fallbacks to current behavior.

Approach:
1) Add a lightweight sidecar process (go) that exposes a local unix socket and accepts compact binary span buffers from language SDKs. SDKs switch to a single nonblocking write of a preallocated buffer on hot path.
2) Sidecar performs deferred batch coalescing, tail-based sampling scans, enriches spans with node metadata, and does JSON serialization and export to the existing tracing backend.
3) Implement per-route adaptive sampling rules: manager publishes rules via config service; sidecar keeps local rule cache and uses incoming span attributes (route, customer_tier, error_flag) to pick sampling target. Rules include deterministic keep probability for specific routes and dynamic up/downscaling knobs.
4) Safety: SDK will still have a configurable synchronous path for critical spans (e.g., SLO violation signals) and a debug flag to force full export. Add circuit-breaker: if sidecar is unresponsive, SDK falls back to current in-process exporter to preserve correctness.

Success criteria / metrics:
- 80%+ reduction in per-request allocations attributed to tracer SDK on instrumented services (measured with pprof).
- p99 latency regression eliminated on critical endpoints compared to baseline under identical load.
- End-to-end trace completion rate for sampled transactions >= baseline for kept traces.
- No increase in dropped spans for high-priority routes (>1% drop rate).

Rollout plan:
- Internal alpha on canary infra for non-customer traffic (2 services) -> measure allocations and tail latency.
- Gradual rollout to low-risk services with sampling rules favoring lower retention.
- Add observability dashboards for sidecar health, buffer queue length, export latency, and sampling decisions.
- If metrics degrade, automatic rollback via feature flag in config manager.

Risks and mitigations:
- Sidecar crashes could delay export: mitigate via SDK fallback and aggressive health check with OOM protection.
- Local IPC regressions on constrained environments: tune buffer sizes and fallback thresholds; provide env var for disabling sidecar.
- Operational complexity of sampling rules: ship with sane default rules and instrument a rule-change audit log.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Service+Sidecar+Span+Aggregator
- Proto/Schema for compact binary buffer: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/tracing-sidecar-schema
updates: 2026-02-20: Spike complete - implemented PoC sidecar prototype in Go; demonstrated nonblocking single-write from Go SDK and Python SDK. Observed ~68% allocation drop in benchmark service (internal load test).

2026-02-25: Security review kickoff - SRE requested capability to run sidecar as non-root and drop network privileges; added plan to support unix socket + explicit chroot/uid. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7881)

2026-03-03: Design review with PM/Observability team - feedback to add per-route denylist and 'always-keep' label for billing-critical traces. Updated design doc to include audit log of sampling decisions.

2026-03-08: Benchmarks against high-QPS endpoint (1000rps) show p99 latency improved by 12% and p50 unchanged; serialization moved off hot path. Need further tuning for exporter backpressure under bursty writes.
2026-03-11: Implemented circuit-breaker and SDK fallback; integration tests added. Preparing canary rollout. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7924
2026-03-12: Canary started on two internal services; initial metrics look good — sidecar queue depth < 5 for 99.9% of intervals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Integration tests pass with SDK fallback exercised. 2) Alpha canary shows >= 60% allocation reduction and no p99 regression. 3) Dashboards report sidecar healthy metrics for 48h. 4) Security checklist items addressed (non-root, socket perms, config ACLs).
qa_plan: Add unit tests for buffer encode/decode and sampling-rule application.
Run load tests with profiling to validate allocation and syscall reductions.
Fault-inject sidecar crashes and verify SDK fallback behavior under load.
Validate per-route sampling by sending tagged requests and confirming keep/drop decisions in audit logs.
notes: Avoids touching hotpath span creation logic except for a single preallocated buffer write.
This complements previous tail-sampling work by centralizing expensive steps and allowing richer sampling heuristics without SDK cost.
Follow-up work: extend sidecar to support batch deduplication and integrate with Redis/HT to coordinate sampling across replicas.
